text: Git branching is an important part of a version control workflow. When developers work on a new feature, they create a separate feature branch. This keeps the main branch clean and stable while changes are being made. Once the work is finished, the feature branch can be merged back into the main branch. Before merging, team members often open a pull request so others can review the code, discuss changes, and catch mistakes. This process improves code quality and teamwork. By using branches and pull requests, teams can work on different tasks at the same time without conflicts. Understanding this workflow helps developers collaborate more effectively and manage their projects safely.
